name: Extradition
overview: The Scriptures present extradition as the act of authorities delivering individuals from one jurisdiction to another for judgment or punishment, as seen when King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt to bring back Urijah, who was then executed (Jeremiah 26:21-23). Similarly, in the New Testament, Saul received letters authorizing him to bind and bring followers of Christ from Damascus to Jerusalem for punishment (Acts 9:2; 9:14; 22:5). These passages illustrate the use of official authority to apprehend and transfer individuals deemed offenders, underscoring the reality of earthly powers administering justice in accordance with their laws.
